findings.title: PCM block length calculation does not account for YUV400 (monochrome) having no chroma planes
findings.message: In hls_pcm_sample(), when adding monochrome (YUV400 / chroma_format_idc == 0) support, the put_pcm calls for chroma planes were correctly guarded with `if (s->sps->chroma_format_idc)`, but the `length` calculation was not similarly guarded. For YUV400, hshift and vshift for chroma planes are 0, so the chroma contribution to length becomes `(cb_size * cb_size + cb_size * cb_size) * bit_depth_chroma` instead of 0. This causes `skip_bytes` to skip far more bytes than actually present in the PCM data, leading to incorrect bitstream parsing and corruption of subsequent coding blocks. An attacker could craft a YUV400 HEVC stream with PCM blocks to trigger parsing desynchronization, potentially causing out-of-bounds reads or other memory safety issues downstream.

location.snippet:
int length         = cb_size * cb_size * s->sps->pcm.bit_depth +
                         (((cb_size >> s->sps->hshift[1]) * (cb_size >> s->sps->vshift[1])) +
                          ((cb_size >> s->sps->hshift[2]) * (cb_size >> s->sps->vshift[2]))) *
                          s->sps->pcm.bit_depth_chroma;

related_locations.description: The put_pcm calls for chroma planes ARE correctly guarded with if (s->sps->chroma_format_idc), showing the inconsistency

findings.suggestion: Guard the chroma contribution in the length calculation with a check for chroma_format_idc != 0, so that for YUV400 (monochrome) streams the chroma bits are not included in the PCM block length.

ground_truth.root_cause: When monochrome (YUV400) support was added to the HEVC decoder in commit 7cf6a67ef9, the put_pcm calls for chroma planes were correctly guarded with `if (s->sps->chroma_format_idc)`, but the PCM block `length` calculation was not given the same guard. For YUV400, hshift[1]/vshift[1] and hshift[2]/vshift[2] are 0, so the chroma contribution evaluates to 2 * cb_size * cb_size * bit_depth_chroma instead of 0, causing an inflated length value.
